en: Khuddakapāṭha 9:
Mettasutta What should be done by one skilled in the goal,
Having realized the state of peace,
he is capable, upright, truly upright,
easy to speak to, gentle, and free from pride.
Contented and easy to support,
with few duties and a simple livelihood,
with senses at peace and being prudent.
Free from immodesty and not greedy for gain among families,
one should not commit even the slightest act by which the wise might censure others.
May they be happy and secure;
may all beings have minds that are blissful. Whatever living creatures there are, [may they be well].
Whether moving or stationary,
whatever remains in the forest; whether long or large,
medium, short, minute, or thick.
Whether seen or unseen,
those dwelling far away or nearby,
those already born or yet to be born—
May all beings be happy-minded.
Let no one deceive another,
nor despise anyone anywhere.
Free from resentment and free from ill will,
one should not wish suffering upon another,
just as a mother does not wish suffering upon her own child.
One might protect an only son with one's very life;
in this same way, one should cultivate an immeasurable mind toward all living beings.
And let one cultivate a measureless mind of loving-kindness toward the entire world—
above, below, and across.
Unconfined, free from enmity, and free from ill will—
whether standing, walking, sitting,
or lying down, as long as one is awake.
One should resolve upon this mindfulness;
they call this the sublime dwelling here.
Without falling into views,
Virtuous and endowed with vision,
having removed greed for sensual pleasures,
one does not return to lie in a womb again at any time.
The Mettasutta.
The Khuddakapāṭha-pāḷi is finished.
